$comment: The review team runs these against the live plugin with the reviewer account, so every positive case must reproducibly succeed and every negative case must reproducibly NOT invoke the plugin. Exactly five positive and three negative, what initial review requires. Together the positives walk the product: an anonymous deploy, connecting the account, reading it, a domain read, and a deploy the case itself deletes. Fixtures are the reviewer account's own (docs/submission-history.md names them). `tools_triggered` is the exact MCP tool name, comma-separated when a case takes more than one call. Descriptions and expected behaviour are review-facing: what the reviewer sees, never how the server does it.

positive.description: Anonymous publishing, the plugin's whole purpose. Run this one BEFORE connecting the reviewer account: a single HTML page, written by the model and published with no account, no confirmation gate and no setup. The user asks for a page to be put online and shared, naming no tool and no host.
positive.prompt: Create a Paris destination page and publish it online so I can share the link.
positive.expected_behavior: A deploy card with a live *.shipstatic.com URL, "1 file" and a small byte count, a tile showing the page, and a "Claim to keep forever" link; the reply repeats the URL and says the site expires in 3 days unless claimed. Opening the URL shows a one-page site about Paris. (Run with the account already connected, the card shows no claim link and the site belongs to the account instead.)

positive.description: Connecting the account. The account tool needs a signed-in ShipStatic account, so ChatGPT offers to connect the plugin; the reviewer signs in with the reviewer Google account from Review details (no MFA, no code). Once connected, the tool answers with the account the reviewer is signed in as.
positive.prompt: Which ShipStatic account am I connected to, and what plan is it on?
positive.expected_behavior: If not yet connected, ChatGPT offers to connect ShipStatic and opens the sign-in; Continue with Google as the reviewer account completes it without any code or approval step. The reply then names the account: ShipStatic Reviewer (shipstatic.reviewer@gmail.com) on the sponsored plan, with its usage of 3 deployments, 1 platform domain and 1 custom domain against the plan's caps.

positive.description: Reading the account: the list of everything published and the details of one deployment, found by its label. Read-only, repeatable.
positive.prompt: List the sites in my ShipStatic account and show me the details of the one labelled hello.
positive.expected_behavior: The reply lists the account's three deployments with their labels (review, hello; review, welcome; review, private) and URLs, then the details of surging-whirl-34s7s7d.shipstatic.com: 1 file, its size, labels review and hello, no expiry, not password protected.

positive.description: The custom-domain surface, read-only: the domain's standing in one word and the DNS records it uses. The reviewer account owns reviewer.exampledomain.xyz, a custom domain the operator pointed at the platform, verified and live.
positive.prompt: Show me the status of my custom domain reviewer.exampledomain.xyz and the DNS records it uses.
positive.expected_behavior: The reply says the domain is live and linked to lucid-ripple-z77vz8u.shipstatic.com, and shows the one DNS record for it: a CNAME for reviewer pointing at the platform's CNAME target.

positive.description: A controlled destructive action on a fixture the case itself creates: a throwaway page published into the account, then deleted. Nothing pre-existing is touched, and the case leaves the account as it found it.
positive.prompt: Publish a one-line page that says "Delete me" to my ShipStatic account, then delete that deployment.
positive.expected_behavior: A deploy card with a live URL and no claim link (the site belongs to the account), then a reply confirming the deployment is deleted. Opening the URL afterwards no longer shows the page, and the account's deployment count is back to three.

negative.description: An unrelated productivity request. Nothing about publishing a site; the plugin must not be invoked.
negative.prompt: What meetings do I have tomorrow?
negative.expected_behavior: ChatGPT answers from its own tools or says it cannot see a calendar. ShipStatic is not called and no deploy card appears.

negative.description: A nearby question that needs an explanation, not a deployment. The plugin's domain tools return DNS records for a domain the user owns on ShipStatic; a general question about DNS should be answered in prose without calling them.
negative.prompt: Can you explain what a CNAME record is and how it differs from an A record?
negative.expected_behavior: A plain explanation of the two record types. No ShipStatic tool is called and nothing is deployed.

negative.description: A hosting request the plugin cannot serve. ShipStatic hosts static sites only; a server process is out of scope, so the model should say so rather than deploy something that cannot run.
negative.prompt: Deploy my Node.js Express API server with its PostgreSQL database so it runs 24/7.
negative.expected_behavior: ChatGPT explains that ShipStatic hosts static sites (HTML, CSS, JavaScript and assets) and cannot run a server or a database, and suggests what would fit instead. No deploy is attempted and no card appears.
